thread:
Harpreet: Quick announcement: we're launching official WebAssembly (WASM) client support for the Redwood SDKs (browser + edge). This aims to give low-latency embedding and lightweight generate clients that run without server-side SDKs. Docs + preview bundles live next week.

Nora: TL;DR for docs teams: add a new "WASM client" guide, security checklist, and integration recipes (React, Service Worker, Edge Functions). We'll include a short migration path for teams using old browser polyfills.

Ilya: Infra notes: hosted endpoints will accept the same API keys but we recommend short-lived tokens from the session endpoint for browser flows. We'll publish an example token minting flow (JWT with 5m expiry).

Zoe: Security summary: by default browser bundles DO NOT include any persistent telemetry tokens and CORS policies restrict origins. We also added a client-side rate limiter and strict-origin referrer checks. Important: warn customers not to embed long-lived secrets.

Harpreet: SDK behavior: the WASM package exposes a small surface: init(config), generate(opts), embeddings(text). It uses a streaming-friendly fetch wrapper and supports chunked responses. Example (browser):
```js
const client = await RedwoodWasm.init({ endpoint: '/v1', token: await mintShortLivedToken() });
const it = await client.generate({ prompt: 'Summarize X', stream: true });
for await (const chunk of it) console.log(chunk.delta);
```

Nora: Docs will include: quickstart, token-minting recipe, CORS & CSP guidance, a compatibility table (old polyfills -> WASM), and known limitations (no local KV cache, sequence-length caps in browser). Draft to #docs-review in 48h.

Ilya: Platform will add a "WASM client" user-agent metric and a small quota to protect hosted capacity while teams experiment. Dedicated customers can disable the quota via admin.

Zoe: Compliance note: we'll ship a short SBOM for the WASM bundle and a signed checksum for release artifacts. Security scanned and approved for staging; production roll after one week of canary traffic.

Harpreet: Rollout plan:
- Day 0: announce + docs draft.
- Day 4: preview npm packages and WASM bundles (alpha).
- Day 7: docs + example apps published.
- Day 14: canary on 2% of hosted traffic.
- Day 21+: GA if no major issues.

Nora: Add a short FAQ: "Can I run private models in WASM?" Answer: Not yet; WASM client talks to Redwood endpoints. We're exploring local model runtimes in a later phase.

Harpreet: Please react with :rocket: if you want invites to the preview or leave questions here.
